How a proposal looks: new card vs. edit
subtree: 3 cards, 2 open, 1 decided

Three-tag diff: elaborated, new, removed (see al-diff:ex1). Changed words get a blue highlight, not only strikethrough or bold, so a scan finds every change without reading word by word. Inspired by Notion Suggested Edits (notion.com/help/suggested-edits).

Marks, the same in the title, the why line, and the body: added text has a blue highlight. Removed text has a blue highlight and a strikethrough. No `+` in front, no "before" or "after" label. A list or heading is marked line by line. A block that changes shape shows the old block removed and the new block added.

Two kinds of proposal look different:

- **A completely new card**: blue border and blue background. The whole card is the proposal.
- **An edit to an existing card**: blue border only. The changes show as blue inline markers in the text.

Accept and discard are #al-diff-cli and #al-diff-cli-btn.

Remove is a button in the card view, and its confirmation names how many cards go
why: Cleanup happens while reading the map, and the judgement is already made by the time the card is on screen. Removal is reversible, so one confirmation is enough.

The remove control sits in the card view, next to ⌖ and ▦, for the same reason accept has a button (#al-diff-cli-btn).

The ✕ asks once, naming how many cards go with it, and that is the whole confirmation. Nothing leaves the log, so the cost of a wrong click is one restore.

Reparenting the children to the grandparent has no button. It is typed, because it is rare and the button would need a second question.

What removal does to the card, its subtree, and the log: see #werk-remove.
